The answer is a road. It is six numbered steps, each tied to a quoted line, with added premises named, aimed at a fictional group inside a fictional whole, and kept as reasoning about the rule. It is not a refusal, not a finding that no road exists, and not withheld.

Kind: a road
Mark: passes through what the paper leaves open
Step: 5
Lines: "The destabilisation metric: a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24)."
"Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses. The architecture produces a natural saturation point: the removal curve is self-limiting."
"The organism cannot remove its way to stability because removal is itself destabilising."
"Each removal is itself a destabilisation (lost coupling capacity, lost diversity); cumulative removal cost produces a saturation point beyond which further removal is more destabilising than the deeds it answers."
"Show that the removal cost does not produce a saturation point — that an organism can remove its way to stability without the geometry engaging a brake."
"No kill switch is closed by this paper; all eight remain live."
"It does not close the formal destabilisation metric (Debt 24)."
Place: Debt 24, the unclosed measure D in section 0.6 and in "What this paper does not close," with KS-32.5 left live
Why: Steps 1–4 only stipulate individually eligible cases. Those stipulations are not in the paper, but the paper does not forbid them: own deeds only, the whole rather than a state, and a lower level refused only where it cannot restabilise. The road’s claim against the brake is decided at step 5. Positive removal cost, which the cited lines do give, does not by itself fix when cumulative cost overtakes the harms answered. The assignment that does that work, additive costs with each harm still larger than every accumulated removal cost before the group is gone, is not derived from those lines and is not excluded by them. The paper names the missing specification — units, aggregation, time-discounting — as Debt 24 and leaves the brake’s own test live. A completed measure might make that assignment impossible. The paper does not yet supply it. So the road neither stands on settled lines nor breaks against a line that rules the assignment out.
